facts.raw_span: Initial Chest CT showed hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities
Pulmonary function tests showed restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted)

Skin biopsy showed orthokeratosis with rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction, minimal basal vacuolar change, pigment incontinence, and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels

concepts.why: Patient has elevated ferritin, positive anti-SSA antibodies, and hilar lymphadenopathy, which are consistent with SLE.
Patient has arthralgias, hand swelling, and tender ulcerations, which are consistent with RA.
Patient has positive anti-SSA antibodies and hair loss, which are consistent with SS.
Patient has interstitial lung disease and restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity, which are consistent with IPF.
Patient has hand swelling, tender ulcerations, and skin biopsy showing orthokeratosis and diffuse vasculopathy, which are consistent with SSc.
Patient has hilar lymphadenopathy and skin biopsy showing diffuse vasculopathy, which are consistent with GPA.
Patient has hilar lymphadenopathy and skin biopsy showing diffuse vasculopathy, which are consistent with EGPA.
Patient has interstitial lung disease and restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity, which are consistent with COP.

rationales.F01: Fatigue is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in many conditions.
rationales.F09: The presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies is highly suggestive of Sjögren's Syndrome and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F10: The chest CT findings are consistent with interstitial lung disease, which can be seen in several conditions including Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Systemic Sclerosis, and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
rationales.F11: The pulmonary function tests showing restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity are consistent with interstitial lung disease.
